🎥🎬: The Boondocks (2005–2014)

Huey and Riley Freeman are two very different brothers who move with their grandfather, Robert, from Chicago to the mostly white suburb of Woodcrest. Huey is a politically aware revolutionary who constantly questions society, while Riley is obsessed with gangsta culture and dreams of becoming a rapper.

Their lives quickly become chaotic as they clash with their grandfather, neighbors, and the bizarre characters around them. Through sharp satire, outrageous situations, and plenty of controversy, the Freeman family takes on race, politics, culture, celebrity, and American society.

source_details.title: The Boondocks
source_details.synopsis: The Boondocks is an American adult animated black sitcom created by Aaron McGruder for Cartoon Network's late-night programming block Adult Swim, based on his manga-influenced comic strip of the same name. The series focuses on a Black American family, the Freemans, and their experiences in the fictional, predominantly white suburb of Woodcrest. The perspective offered by this mixture of cultures, lifestyles, social classes, stereotypes, viewpoints and racialized identities provides for much of the series' satire, comedy, and conflict.
